locator.section: 8.2 Product stability -- Charge competition in OE(+.) decompositions: Stevenson's Rule

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.4, second branch, arrow labeled 'alpha'; instantiated with x = n-butyl. Radical-site (alpha) cleavage driven by the carbonyl oxygen radical cation: the odd electron on O6 forms the second C5-O6 pi bond (acylium CH3-C(triple bond)O+, m/z 43) while the C(butyl)-C(=O) sigma bond breaks and the butyl group departs as the neutral radical .C4H9. The page tabulates: n = 100%, s = 100%, t = 35% -- the acylium dominates for n-/s-butyl but is overtaken by t-C4H9+ once the tert-butyl-cation IE (6.7 eV) drops below that of the acetyl fragment (printed 7.0 eV). Book draws 0 arcs (summary equation); the three balanced fishhooks (O6 odd electron -> C5-O6 pi, upgrading C=O to the C(triple)O of the acylium; one electron of the C4-C5 bond -> that same pi; the second electron of C4-C5 -> the departing butyl radical) are the standard radical-site alpha-cleavage flow, reconstructed here. This is the direct homolog of the acetone alpha-cleavage of Eq 4.13 (the schema example).

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_4 (equation 8.4). MISMATCH: the rule's substrate is an ETHER (no carbonyl), and it cleaves a C-C bond to give a butyl radical cation plus an oxygen cation, RHS charge +2 -- charge-non-conserving and dropped by the conservation guardrail. It forms NO acylium (there is no C=O to upgrade to C(triple)O) and therefore does not reproduce this alpha branch at all. See rule_mismatches.

Book prints '100%' relative abundance under CH3CO+ for x = n (also 100% for s, 35% for t). observed_mz 43.0178 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of C2H3O+ (acylium); the page prints only the % abundances and the fragment IE (7.0 eV), no m/z.
